title: Phase-field crawlers that grow on a consumed nutrient and divide: a single founder gives 4 generations of crawling, dividing cells (3 seeds), with matched ablations for division and motility
summary: world.py is the Ziebert-Aranson crawler (positive control 20261025T0641) extended with per-body content V grown by uptake of a regrowing nutrient, a weak finite-range (Gaussian, ell=10) area penalty inside bodies that tears oversized bodies, nutrient-modulated actin production beta(n), maintenance per body and shedding of content on retraction. From one planted, kicked founder the population grows to 6-15 cells by t=600: crescent crawlers that move several body lengths, grow, pinch into dumbbells and separate (strips/). labkit: max generation 3/4/4 on seeds 0/1/2, persistent splits 4/11/10, merge/split 0.17/0.20/0.07, max body lengths travelled 40/7.9/11.4. Matched ablations on the same parameters: lamOK=0 never divides (the founder overgrows its patch and dies by t~80, 2 seeds); chi=0 still divides (gen 6) but no body moves more than 2.6 body lengths and the population jams into a crystal; shed=0 (content conserved exactly) booms into worm-like masses that crash into a static lattice with merge/split 0.49-0.62 and gen 1; shed=1 gives one crawler that never divides.

claims.statement: From one planted founder, discrete crawling cells (I) move as keratocyte-like crescents for several body lengths with the body plan kept and no imposed field (M; the nutrient gradient they follow is their own depletion), and divide repeatedly into separate cells of the same kind (D): max generation 4 on seeds 1 and 2 and 3 on seed 0, merge/split <= 0.20.
claims.track: seed 1, track 9 (pack/seed1/lineage.png; strips/strip_s1_t9.png): born at generation 3 (0->2->6->9) at frame 40 (t=100), crawls 7.2 body lengths (metrics motion_top id 9), rounds and pinches at frame 100 and splits at frame 101 into tracks 28 and 29 (generation 4), which separate.

controls_run.D: ablation_lamOK0/ (lamOK=0, seeds 0 and 1: no split, founder dies by t~80)
controls_run.M: ablation_chi0/ (chi=0, seed 1: max 2.6 body lengths, vs 7.9 with chi=2 on the same seed)

claims.bd_control: not run; the division operator is a finite-range (nonlocal) area penalty and motility is advection along a polarization field, but no Laplacian-only twin was tested

limitations: Seeds differ only in the founder's position and kick direction (the dynamics have no noise), so seed-to-seed variation is limited. Motility is strongest in the first generations; after food runs out (t>~350-450) the cells round up and freeze into a lattice of starving cells, and the deepest-generation division in seed 2 (strips/strip_s2_t31.png) is by a round, nearly stationary cell. No deaths after the founder phase were counted, so there is no turnover. Body content V is a per-body scalar carried by overlap (bookkeeping, not a field); division needs the finite-range penalty, a nonlocal operator. The shedding cost was introduced after finding that my earlier overlap bookkeeping leaked content in proportion to motion (sighting 20261025T0720 used the leaky version); the shed sweep 0/0.2/0.5/1 shows the regime needs it. Labelled with --threshold 0.25 (in META) so that pinched-off pieces are tracked from birth; at 0.5 the tracker reported many nucleations. Not tested: dt/2 or grid refinement.
